production.note: US model years, from Kelley Blue Book (a database): the GT page lists model years 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023, with one trim, "Coupe 2D", "612 @ 7500 RPM". The GTS that followed is a separate model. McLaren's release: "Order now for delivery towards the end of 2019"; Carscoops (Sergiu Tudose, 15 May 2019): "Pricing in the U.S. starts from $210,000" with deliveries "towards the end of 2019" (carscoops-gt).

body.note: Two-seat fixed-roof grand tourer with a rear luggage hatch; coupe body only.

displacementL.note: 3,994 cc: Top Gear spec page "Engine Capacity: 3,994cc"; McLaren's release says "4.0-litre".

drivetrain.note: Top Gear spec page: "Drive Train: Rear Wheel Drive" (mid-engined).

transmission.note: "7-speed SSG transmission" (McLaren Seamless Shift Gearbox, recorded as a DCT as in other McLaren records). No manual.

powerHp.note: Quote (McLaren release reproduced by conceptcarz, "Source - McLaren"): "With 620PS from its 4.0-litre, twin-turbocharged V8 engine, the power-to-weight ratio of the superlight new McLaren GT is a remarkable 405PS-per-tonne." 620 x 0.98632 = 612 hp, so powerStandard is DIN PS. Carscoops: "612 HP (620 PS)" (carscoops-gt); KBB: "612 @ 7500 RPM" (kbb-gt).

weightLb.note: Coupe, 7-speed SSG (the only transmission). Quote (McLaren release): "At 1,530kg (DIN), the McLaren GT is more than 130kg lighter than its closest core competitor". DIN kerb weight, not EU; 1,530 x 2.20462 = 3,373 lb. Carscoops prints "1,530 kg (3,373 lbs)" (carscoops-gt) and Top Gear's spec page "Minimum Kerbweight: 1,530kg" (topgear-gt-spec). No US-specific figure was found.
